canonicalization.digest_target: the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 canonicalized protocol.json document
canonicalization.self_reference_rule: canonical_contract_sha256 is batch metadata and is not stored inside protocol.json
canonicalization.verification_rule: servers and clients MUST reject a contract batch when the received digest differs from the allowlisted canonical digest

supported_protocol_versions.name: legacy_tree_projection
supported_protocol_versions.description: Protocol 1 writes are accepted only through the LEGACY epoch-0 adapter. They do not invent contract batch metadata.

supported_protocol_versions.name: authoritative_folders_legacy
supported_protocol_versions.description: Protocol 2 may use stable folder identities while a project remains LEGACY, but it does not claim released contract provenance.

supported_protocol_versions.name: contract_batch_id_tree
supported_protocol_versions.description: Every protocol 3 write uses an immutable contract batch. Structural writes use atomic_structure_commit and document body writes use document_commit.

folders_authoritative.meaning: Folder existence and identity are represented by stable folder_id rows.

tree_order_ids.meaning: tree_order child entries reference folder_id or document_id.

legacy_tree_folder_projection.meaning: Name-based tree projection is permitted only in LEGACY epoch 0.

immutable_batch_contract_metadata.meaning: Every contract-native operation references one immutable batch carrying complete released-contract metadata.

operation_state_events.meaning: Operation state is derived from an append-only event sequence.

storage_name_v1.meaning: Storage-name collision keys use Unicode 15.0.0 NFKC_Casefold and the storage-name-v1 rejection rules.

document_commit_v1.meaning: Document create, body update, delete, and restore use the normative document_commit wire with one immutable intent per atomic batch.

atomic_structure_commit.meaning: The server validates and commits one ordered structure batch in one transaction or applies nothing.

contract_allowlist_validation.meaning: The server maps canonical contract digests to permitted protocol versions, capabilities, and builds.

project_mode_migration_lock.meaning: The server serializes migration epochs and rejects stale or concurrent migration writers.

folder_tombstones.meaning: The server retains folder identity, parent, revision, and deletion state.

id_tree_validation.meaning: The server rejects missing, deleted, cross-project, cyclic, or duplicate ID tree references.

legacy_epoch_zero_adapter.meaning: The server records honest LEGACY_EPOCH_0 provenance without synthesizing unavailable contract metadata.

storage_name_v1.meaning: The server computes and compares the same storage-name-v1 UTF-8 collision key as clients.

document_commit_v1.meaning: The server validates and commits one complete document snapshot in one transaction or applies nothing.

capability_version_rules.declaration_rule: A client MUST NOT declare a capability when sync_protocol_version is less than that capability's since_protocol.
capability_version_rules.required_rule: A writer MUST declare every required client capability for its selected protocol version.
capability_version_rules.server_rule: A server MUST advertise every required server capability before accepting writes for the selected protocol version.
capability_version_rules.unknown_capability_rule: Unknown or not-yet-available capabilities are rejected with CAPABILITY_MISMATCH.
capability_version_rules.batch_rule: Protocol 3 requires CONTRACT_BATCH provenance; protocols 1 and 2 require LEGACY_EPOCH_0 provenance and MUST NOT fabricate a batch_id.

server_rules: A CONTRACT_BATCH operation MUST reference exactly one existing batch.
The authenticated writer and writer_device_id MUST be bound when the batch is created.
Contract metadata and batch_payload_sha256 MUST NOT be mutated.
An identical transport retry MUST reuse batch_id and operation_id.
A rebase creates a new batch_id and operation_id because its base revision and payload digest differ.

rules: The original intent and its attempts remain unchanged.
The rebased operation_id and batch_id MUST differ from the original values.
supersedes_operation_id MUST identify the conflicted original operation.
A superseded event is appended to the original after the new intent is durably created.
Replay processes the original event stream before the new intent and follows supersedes_operation_id exactly once.

event.ordering_rule: event_sequence starts at 1 and is contiguous and unique per operation_id.
event.idempotency_rule: event_id is globally idempotent; an identical replay returns the existing event and a changed event is EVENT_ID_REUSED.

rules: Current state MUST be derived by folding contiguous events in event_sequence order over the immutable intent.
Attempt history MUST NOT be deleted when completion or cancellation occurs.
blocked and conflict events MUST carry a stable error code or blocking operation_id.
A terminal operation rejects later state-changing events with OPERATION_TERMINAL.
The first valid cancel_requested event makes a non-terminal operation cancelled.
An identical cancel_event_id replay returns already_cancelled without appending a second event.
Reusing cancel_event_id with different content is EVENT_ID_REUSED.
Cancellation after completed is rejected with OPERATION_TERMINAL and does not change state.
Cancellation of an already cancelled operation with a new event ID returns already_cancelled and does not append a state-changing event.

migration_validation: Every live folder has a unique folder_id in the project.
Every live document has a unique document_id in the project.
Every parent_folder_id resolves to a live folder in the same project or is null.
Every tombstone retains entity identity and a monotonic revision.
Every ID-based tree reference resolves exactly once.
No live siblings share the same storage-name-v1 UTF-8 collision key.

structure_write_matrix.server_behavior: Accept through the legacy adapter without batch metadata.
Accept stable folder identities while retaining LEGACY epoch-0 provenance.
Validate the released contract batch and use atomic_structure_commit.
Require the active migration epoch, lock ownership, and atomic_structure_commit.
Atomically apply the complete ordered structure batch or reject it.
Reject content and structure writes with PROTOCOL_TOO_OLD.
Reject content and structure writes with PROTOCOL_TOO_OLD.

atomic_structure_commit.atomic_boundary: one request containing one immutable batch and its complete ordered_intents array
atomic_structure_commit.ordering_rule: sequence starts at 1, is contiguous, and is the sole apply and replay order.
atomic_structure_commit.payload_digest_rule: batch_payload_sha256 is SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes of ordered_intents.
atomic_structure_commit.success_rule: Success returns committed or replayed for the entire batch and one result per ordered intent.
atomic_structure_commit.failure_rule: Any validation or apply failure rolls back the transaction, returns applied=false, and returns no successful intent result.
atomic_structure_commit.replay_rule: An identical batch_id and batch_payload_sha256 returns status=replayed with result fields identical to the original committed response; a different payload is BATCH_ID_REUSED.
atomic_structure_commit.partial_apply_rule: A partial apply MUST NOT be represented as success and MUST be rolled back.

document_commit.atomic_boundary: one request containing one immutable batch and exactly one document intent with sequence 1
document_commit.ordering_rule: ordered_intents contains exactly one item and its sequence is 1; document history order is the server-committed result_revision order.
document_commit.payload_digest_rule: payload_sha256 is SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes of payload; batch_payload_sha256 is SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes of ordered_intents; content_sha256 is SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 content bytes and content_byte_count is their length.
document_commit.success_rule: Success returns committed or replayed for the entire batch and exactly one result matching the request operation_id and document_id. An empty content string is an intentional write with byte count 0 and SHA-256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855.
document_commit.failure_rule: Any authentication, capability, digest, name, revision, structure-barrier, or apply failure rolls back the transaction, returns applied=false, and returns no result.
document_commit.replay_rule: An identical batch_id and batch_payload_sha256 returns status=replayed with result fields identical to the original committed response after response loss or restart; a different payload is BATCH_ID_REUSED; a reused operation_id with different immutable intent is OPERATION_ID_REUSED.
document_commit.partial_apply_rule: A missing, extra, mismatched, or partial document result MUST NOT be represented as success and a client MUST NOT apply it.
intent_rules: create requires base_revision 0, is_deleted false, and a document_id that does not exist; it creates identity, name, parent, structure revision 1, and the complete content snapshot atomically.
update requires base_revision greater than 0 and is_deleted false; name, parent_folder_id, and structure_revision must equal the live server row and only the content snapshot changes.

delete requires base_revision greater than 0 and is_deleted true; name, parent_folder_id, structure_revision, content, content digest, and content byte count must equal the live server row so deletion cannot silently alter content.

restore requires base_revision greater than 0 and is_deleted false; name, parent_folder_id, structure_revision, content, content digest, and content byte count must equal the tombstone; a later update performs any body edit.
Document rename and move use atomic_structure_commit and must complete before a later document update names their resulting structure_revision.
A tree_order removal must commit before document delete; document create or restore must commit before tree_order adds the document_id.
document_commit.structure_barrier_rule: Except for create, document_commit never changes name, parent_folder_id, or structure_revision. A stale structure_revision is rejected with STRUCTURE_REVISION_CONFLICT.

storage_name_normalization.input_scope: one folder or file name segment, never a path
steps: Reject U+0000, U+0001 through U+001F, U+007F, slash, and backslash.
Apply Unicode Normalization Form KC using Unicode 15.0.0.
Apply Unicode 15.0.0 Default Case Folding without locale.
Apply Unicode Normalization Form KC again.
Remove every trailing U+0020 SPACE or U+002E FULL STOP.
Reject an empty result, dot, or dot-dot.
Take the substring before the first U+002E FULL STOP and reject Windows device basenames CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 through COM9, and LPT1 through LPT9.
Encode the remaining string as UTF-8; these exact bytes are the sibling collision key.
storage_name_normalization.internal_space_policy: Internal Unicode whitespace is preserved subject to NFKC_Casefold.
storage_name_normalization.comparison_policy: Compare collision-key UTF-8 bytes for exact equality.

legacy_migration.unknown_metadata_policy: Unknown historical build, protocol, digest, batch, or device values MUST remain null or absent with unknown_reason PRE_CONTRACT_HISTORY; implementations MUST NOT invent values.
legacy_migration.history_policy: Pre-contract rows remain in their existing ledger or an explicitly namespaced legacy ledger and are not rewritten into contract batches.
legacy_migration.enforcement_boundary: The successful server-locked LEGACY to MIGRATING transition creates migration_epoch 1 and contract_enforcement_started_at. Every later write requires protocol 3 CONTRACT_BATCH provenance.
legacy_migration.promotion_rule: Promotion is manual. Validation success permits an explicit MIGRATING to ID_BASED transition; it never causes automatic promotion.
legacy_migration.failure_rule: A failed migration remains MIGRATING with diagnostics and is not automatically downgraded.
legacy_migration.legacy_invariant_scope: Immutable batch invariants apply only to CONTRACT_BATCH operations. Legacy rows remain subject to identity, authorization, and data-integrity checks that can be proven from recorded fields.

server_invariants.rule: Revisions are positive and strictly increase per entity after create.
operation_id is globally idempotent: an identical replay returns the original result and a different immutable intent is OPERATION_ID_REUSED.
A live relative path is owned by at most one document_id within a project.
In authoritative folder modes, folder identity comes only from folders.
In ID_BASED, tree_order controls order only and every reference resolves to a live entity in the same project.
Deletion is represented by a tombstone; absence alone is not deletion.
A project sync mode never changes automatically.
A protocol 3 structure batch is all-or-nothing at the atomic_structure_commit request boundary.
Every CONTRACT_BATCH operation is traceable to immutable writer, build, protocol, version, capability, payload, and canonical contract digest metadata.
Folder parent relationships remain within one project and contain no cycle.
Operation projections are reproducible from immutable intent plus contiguous append-only events and attempts.
Sibling storage-name collisions are decided only by exact storage-name-v1 UTF-8 collision-key equality.
A protocol 3 document body write is all-or-nothing at the document_commit request boundary and never changes existing document structure.

validation_order: Resolve canonical_contract_sha256 in the server allowlist.
Verify contract_version and sync_protocol_version match that entry.
Verify every declared capability exists and its since_protocol is not greater than sync_protocol_version.
Verify all capabilities required by the selected protocol are declared.
Verify project_sync_mode and minimum_write_protocol permit the requested intent.
Validate batch metadata, operation intent, revisions, storage names, and invariants.
Apply or reject the complete atomic boundary.

evidence_policy.public_source: Reproducible Git commits and repository files may support implementation claims.
evidence_policy.preserved_local_database: A preserved database is separate evidence and MUST include an accessible artifact identifier and digest before another platform claims to have verified it.
evidence_policy.operational_database: Repository migrations MUST NOT be described as deployed state unless the operational migration ledger was inspected read-only.
evidence_policy.unknown_evidence: Unavailable operational or preserved evidence MUST be reported as not verified.
